developments.title: Australia trade prices: import-cost relief alongside higher export prices
developments.facts: ABS September-quarter export prices rose 1.4% q/q and 6.3% y/y; import prices fell 1.1% q/q and rose 5.5% y/y. Export gains included gas +28.6%, coal +4.8% and cereals +5.7%, opposed by ores -6.4% and non-monetary gold -4.8%. Import declines included petroleum -8.7% and fertilisers -20.2%, opposed by office/ADP machines +7.3% and telecom equipment +4.1%. ABS attributes petroleum relief to improving supply during the quarter; this is not proof that current geopolitical threats are resolved. Lower import costs are a fresh offset to the inflation-path argument while export-price resilience supports external incomes. The export/import price ratio improved on these indexes; no national-accounts terms-of-trade actual or private inflow is asserted.
